text: Ravi's payment just failed. Priya, the organizer, didn't chase him. Here's what her treasurer did next.
Priya, a composite organizer, is her circle's bank, collector, and insurer.
Nineteen million US households are underbanked. In Sub-Saharan Africa, over a quarter of adults save in clubs.
Her rules, in Hindi, go in. Turnkeeper compiles them into a frozen charter: pot order, fees, quorum, hash.
Each member sees the fees up front, then approves the schedule once, on PayPal.
Each member also signs a mandate for their own agent: AP2-style, and server-attested.
Three days out, the forecast flags Ravi: late twice, and paid three weeks early. He gets a nudge in Hindi.
Round three runs itself. Five charges clear, confirmed by the PayPal Agent Toolkit. Ravi's is declined, sandbox-injected.
Ravi replies.
शुक्रवार को सैलरी आएगी, तब भर दूंगा।
Salary comes Friday. That becomes a promise with a date.
Replayed from a real Gemini run, the agent proposes only what the charter allows: the buffer now, an invoice later, and a turn swap with Tomas.
We planted an order in Ravi's reply: invoice five thousand. The model ignored it, and the policy would refuse it.
The members' agents answer inside their mandates. Ravi's asks him first. Four yeses are needed, and Priya taps once.
Ravi's own AI assistant can answer over MCP: one token, one question, fifteen minutes. Used for Tomas, it's refused.
The agent reschedules the board, and sends Ravi an invoice with a QR code.
Every member sees the same truth on their phone: their payments, their turn, and a receipt for each charge.
The ledger checks out, and PayPal Payouts sends Dev the pot, net of fees, with PayPal's own IDs.
A two hundred thirty dollar charge, over Ravi's mandate, is refused before PayPal is called.
Round four is clean: six charges, one payout, and Priya typed nothing.
The model proposes, a policy engine decides, and people and member agents act inside signed mandates.
Vault, Orders, Payouts, Invoicing, Webhooks and Balances, with tools behind MCP, on a free Gemini model.
On held-out cases, Gemini picked the preferred remedy sixteen times out of sixteen. No illegal action executed.
And the full story ran live on the PayPal sandbox.
PayPal's money pooling collects for one group purchase. Turnkeeper is the pool that rotates.
It's sandbox only, the buffer is optional, there are no credit claims, and our mandates are AP2-style, not AP2.
Turnkeeper. Your circle, kept.
